artworks.title: Circe Invidiosa
artworks.description: Waterhouse paints Circe poisoning the bay for Scylla — the jealous revenge that answers Glaucus' refusal. The sea-god himself is off-canvas, but the green pour is the climax of his Ovidian love story (Art Gallery of South Australia).

music.title: Scylla et Glaucus
music.description: Leclair's tragédie en musique gives the Anthedonian sea-god the title role — Glaucus, Scylla, and Circe's revenge for the Paris Opéra.

popCulture.title: Metamorphoses
popCulture.creator: Ovid
popCulture.description: Books 13–14: the fisherman tastes the herb, becomes a blue-green god, loves Scylla, and watches Circe poison the strait.

popCulture.title: Glaucus
popCulture.description: Semi-divine sea-dweller of Anthedon — distinct from the Lycian captain, forever bound to Scylla's transformation.
